attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post. The quoted phrase about data as a substitute for intelligence is his description of the idea he opposes, and he endorses the causal assertion around it.

semantics.note: The causal link is stated firmly ('has led us'). The proposition keeps the hedge 'apparent' on the bubble.

contract.note: The contract requires proof that the boom is a bubble, but Marcus hedged that part with 'apparent'. Holding hedged language to a firm test goes beyond his words. Only the firm part, that the scaling idea drove the situation, should be graded.

evidence.note: A company disclosure (Altman blog, Feb 2025) that ties spending logic to scaling laws. It shows one firm's rationale, not that scaling was the main driver across the industry, and says nothing on a bubble.
Sutskever says scaling dominated the field and the number of companies in it. That fits the causal story, but it does not separate scaling from other investment drivers or show a bubble.

reviews.rationale: The evidence shows scaling was used to justify AI spending. It does not establish that scaling was the main driver as opposed to demand or competition, and the packet admits no source settles the bubble question. Even with the hedged part set aside, the firm causal part is not settled by the evidence.

attribution.note: Marcus's own concluding statement in his post.

semantics.note: A firm necessity claim ('going to need') with its antecedent kept. The surrounding text is partly prescriptive, but this sentence asserts a requirement, not just a recommendation.

contract.note: Requiring a demonstrated AGI, then evidence of necessity, follows from 'if' and 'need'. Reading 'learn something' as substantive cognitive insight is a judgement call, but a reasonable one. AGI has no definition, so the result turns on interpretation.

evidence.note: ARC Prize (Sept 2026) explicitly declines to call Astra AGI. The antecedent stays unverified. It says nothing about whether cognitive insights are necessary.

reviews.rationale: This is a conditional with no deadline. No verified AGI exists in the evidence, so the antecedent has not occurred and the claim cannot be scored yet. No conclusive event meets the early-resolution rule.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words about his own earlier prediction.

semantics.note: In context, 'it' means achieving general intelligence by scaling LLMs. Only the past-tense 'It didn't' is graded. The permanent 'never' is rightly left out.

contract.note: Reading 'work' as reaching AGI, not as producing capability gains, is the ordinary reading given his stated target. It is not stretched either way.

evidence.note: Business Insider, Aug 2025: Altman says GPT-5 falls short of AGI as most people define it.
Sutskever, Nov 2025: 100x more scale would not transform things, and the field is back to research.
Vinyals (DeepMind) reports big pre-training gains. That is capability progress, not a claim that AGI was reached, so it does not contradict the claim.

reviews.rationale: Under the contract's reading, leading proponents of scaling acknowledged before the post that scaled LLMs had not reached AGI, and Sutskever doubted that scale alone would get there. The counter-context shows continued gains but no claim of AGI.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words. The 'unwelcomed' aside is biographical and rightly left ungraded.

semantics.note: 'Started to come around' is a weak quantifier: a shift has begun, not a consensus. The proposition keeps that.

contract.note: Reading 'come around' as prominent voices accepting the limits of scaling, without having to credit Marcus, is ordinary and fair. Using 2025 as the period is reasonable.

evidence.note: Lambda's write-up of NeurIPS 2025 (the conference ended before the post; published before the evaluation date) says the field is moving away from 'just scale it'. This is one firm's view, published on its company blog.
The same write-up calls 'what got us here won't get us there' a common refrain about LLMs.
Sutskever, Nov 2025, publicly doubts that more scale alone will transform things.
The field is openly polarized. That is consistent with a shift that has only started, and it is not a broad rejection of the critique.

reviews.rationale: Prominent researchers and accounts of NeurIPS 2025 show a visible move toward accepting that scaling has limits. That meets the claim's modest 'started to come around'. The polarization in e4 fits a shift that has begun, not a finished one.
